definitions.title: Radian Measure of Angles
definitions.statement: The radian measure of a central angle in a circle of radius r that subtends an arc of length s is given by theta = s/r. A full rotation of 360 degrees corresponds to 2*pi radians.
conditions: Arc length s and radius r must be measured in identical linear units
Calculus formulas for trigonometric functions require angle inputs to be measured strictly in radians
definitions.explanation: Radian measure is dimensionless, making it the natural mathematical measure for calculus where trigonometric functions are differentiated and integrated without artificial conversion factors.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Always work in radians when computing calculus derivatives or limits.

definitions.title: The Six Basic Trigonometric Functions
definitions.statement: For any real angle theta, let (x, y) be the coordinates of the terminal point on the unit circle x^2 + y^2 = 1. The six trigonometric functions are defined by their unit circle projections.
conditions: tan theta and sec theta are defined for theta != pi/2 + k*pi (where x != 0)
cot theta and csc theta are defined for theta != k*pi (where y != 0)
definitions.explanation: Sine and cosine are bounded on [-1, 1] and defined for all real numbers. The other four functions have periodic vertical asymptotes where their respective denominators vanish.
definitions.keyTakeaway: sin and cos have domain R; tan, sec, csc, cot have periodic domain singularities.

definitions.title: Periodicity and General Sinusoids
definitions.statement: A function f is periodic with period p > 0 if f(x + p) = f(x) for all x in its domain. The sine, cosine, secant, and cosecant functions have fundamental period 2*pi; tangent and cotangent have period pi.
conditions: B != 0 determines horizontal compression and frequency
definitions.explanation: Graphing any general sinusoidal wave involves identifying the amplitude |A|, period 2*pi/|B|, horizontal phase shift C, and vertical displacement D.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Period of sin(Bx) is 2pi/|B|; period of tan(Bx) is pi/|B|.

definitions.title: The Fundamental Pythagorean Identities
definitions.statement: For all values of theta where the functions are defined, the sum of the squares of cosine and sine equals 1. Dividing by cos^2(theta) yields the tangent-secant identity; dividing by sin^2(theta) yields the cotangent-cosecant identity.
conditions: Applicable on respective domain domains of tangent, secant, cotangent, cosecant
definitions.explanation: Direct algebraic consequence of the Pythagorean theorem applied to the unit circle x^2 + y^2 = 1.
definitions.keyTakeaway: cos^2 + sin^2 = 1 is the cornerstone for all trigonometric simplifications.

definitions.title: Double-Angle and Half-Angle Reduction Formulas
definitions.statement: The double-angle formulas express trigonometric functions of 2*theta in terms of theta. The half-angle formulas reduce the power of squared trigonometric terms to linear terms.
definitions.explanation: These power-reduction formulas are crucial in integral calculus for evaluating integrals of sin^2(x) and cos^2(x).
definitions.keyTakeaway: Power-reduction formulas convert quadratic trig powers into linear double-angle terms.

definitions.title: The Law of Cosines
definitions.statement: In any triangle with sides of lengths a, b, and c, and opposite angle C, the square of one side equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides minus twice their product times the cosine of the included angle.
conditions: When C = 90 degrees (pi/2 rad), cos C = 0 and the formula reduces to the Pythagorean Theorem c^2 = a^2 + b^2
definitions.explanation: Generalizes the Pythagorean theorem to arbitrary acute and obtuse triangles, frequently utilized in related rates and optimization problems.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Generalization of Pythagorean theorem to any oblique triangle.
